arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE PAPER, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The corpus first prints this person at the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 20, so they are in the town's paper by 1834-07-09 and at no stated time before it; nothing reached says when they came. Last printed 1835-07-29.

lives_at.note: Not attested. NOTHING IS BEING WITHHELD HERE: no source reached says where this person lived, and 52 households in this dataset were already in that position before this one was written.

works_at.note: Not attested as a structure this project models. The trade is documented; the premises are not one of the committed records.

persons.name: Byram King

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as founder, hardware merchant, merchant, school district clerk, stove dealer, at the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 20; the Democrat of 27 May 1835, column 5; the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 2; the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 6; the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 12; the Democrat of 8 July 1835, column 9, and 2 further mention(s). The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `hardware_merchant`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'B. King' and 'BYRA' and 'BYRAM KING' and 'BYRAM KING, Clerk' and 'BYRAM KING.' and 'BYRAM, KING' and 'BYWAM KING' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 20; the Democrat of 27 May 1835, column 5; the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 2; the Democrat of 17 June 1835, column 6; the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 12; the Democrat of 8 July 1835, column 9, and 2 further mention(s). The corpus associates the name with Chicago, South Water Street; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `hardware_merchant` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

resident_research.evidence_for: No reliable record found in the reviewed web, institutional-history, digitized-book, newspaper-index and genealogy-finding-aid searches could be tied to this 1835 Chicago person without relying on the name alone.
resident_research.notes: No candidate fact is asserted unless a source bridges the candidate to the 1835 Chicago record by more than name similarity.
resident_research.summary: Every route to this man is contested in the same way. Fergus 1839 prints 'King, Byram, Jones, King & Co.' and the old-settler notice 'King, Byram, died', but three residents of 1835 meet each entry on the folding rule and at most one is the man printed. The 1840 head 'Byram King' at page 207 line 4 is an L7 candidate with no independent discriminator, and the page falls outside the 210-row serial recovery, so no bridge row can be keyed on it.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Byram King as a hardware merchant at Chicago 8 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
